name: Color
summary: Reported skin color or color intensity -- a commercially relevant, genetics-driven attribute across all four berries, not just a blueberry characteristic.
what_is_it: Color describes the reported hue and intensity of a berry's skin -- for example powder-blue versus near-black blueberries, blush versus gold raspberries and blackberries, or white versus deep-red strawberries.
why_it_matters: Color is a primary visual purchase cue at retail and is often part of a variety's commercial positioning -- novel colors (white strawberries, gold raspberries) can be marketed as a distinct selling point alongside yield and flavor, independent of any measured quality difference.
how_evaluated: Formal color measurement uses colorimeter readings or standardized color charts, but most commercial and marketing descriptions are qualitative (e.g. 'vibrant,' 'deep blue,' 'blush pink') without a cited measurement method.
what_affects_it: Genetics sets the achievable color range and pattern for a variety; ripeness at harvest, sun exposure, and growing-season conditions all influence the color actually observed on a given batch of fruit.
how_to_interpret: A color description in marketing material is a qualitative claim, not a standardized measurement, unless a colorimeter reading or chart reference is cited. Color variation across all four berries is real and commercially relevant -- not just a blueberry-specific consideration -- so do not assume a color claim implies anything about flavor or firmness.
